newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fresenius Medical Care sees 97 profits up.
newsitem.headline: Fresenius Medical Care sees 97 profits up.

text.p: German medical group Fresenius Medical Care said on Wednesday that it saw its 1997 profits growing more strongly than sales and said it expected strong growth in both profits and sales this year.
The group also said it planned an earnings-oriented 1997 dividend to allow shareholders to benefit from the group's business development.

Speaking at the group's first-ever annual shareholder meeting, FMC chairman Gerd Krick told shareholders: "It is our intention to allow you as our shareholders to participate in the expected, positive development of our company."
Fresenius Medical Care, which has bought two dialysis centres in the first quarter of 1997, said it would continue to try and strengthen its position in this sector through further acquisitions.
"Through the further acquisition of dialysis centres we will participate actively in the consolidation process in the United States and consolidate our market leadership," Krick said.
Fresenius Medical Care came into being in September 1996 when German medical products company Fresenius AG merged its dialysis business with National Medical Care, a unit of U.S. group W.R. Grace.
